title.en: Pixel → UV → NDC: Cartesian Coordinates & UV Space Explained
title.vi: Pixel → UV → NDC: Toạ độ Descartes & UV space dễ hiểu

summary.en: Every pixel on your screen has an address. In four minutes, Inko the octopus walks through the three ways graphics writes it down: pixel coordinates, UV and NDC.
summary.vi: Mỗi pixel trên màn hình đều có một địa chỉ. Trong bốn phút, bạch tuộc Inko dẫn bạn qua ba cách đồ hoạ ghi địa chỉ đó: toạ độ pixel, UV và NDC.

en: why every graphics tool assumes perpendicular, evenly spaced axes
Y-up vs Z-up, and right- vs left-handed systems (three.js, glTF, Blender, DirectX, Unity)
why UV always runs from 0 to 1, and why a wrongly flipped texture flips top to bottom, never left to right
the pixel-centre rule u = (x + 0.5) / W, and why gl_FragCoord needs no +0.5
UV to NDC: x = 2u − 1 and y = 1 − 2v
vi: vì sao mọi công cụ đồ hoạ ngầm giả định các trục vuông góc và chia đều
Y-up hay Z-up, hệ thuận tay phải hay tay trái (three.js, glTF, Blender, DirectX, Unity)
vì sao UV luôn chạy từ 0 đến 1, và vì sao texture bị lật sai chỉ lộn theo chiều dọc, không bao giờ lật trái phải
quy tắc tâm pixel u = (x + 0.5) / W, và vì sao gl_FragCoord không cần +0.5
đổi UV sang NDC: x = 2u − 1 và y = 1 − 2v

hook.vi: Mỗi pixel có một địa chỉ

conventions.vi: Y-up hay Z-up, và thuận tay nào

quizzes.question: Graphics tools quietly assume the axes are…
quizzes.explanation: Nothing forces it, but every graphics tool assumes right angles and equal spacing. Breaking that by accident is a classic beginner bug.

quizzes.question: A character stands upright in Blender. Imported into three.js with no conversion, it…
answers: Lies along z, head toward you
quizzes.explanation: Blender is Z-up and three.js is Y-up. Blender's up becomes three.js's +z, which points out of the screen.

quizzes.question: Which convention does three.js use?
quizzes.explanation: three.js has +y up, +x right and +z toward the viewer: right-handed. Blender is Z-up; DirectX and Unity are traditionally left-handed.

quizzes.question: You swap a 16 px texture for an 8192 px one. What must change in the shader's UV code?
quizzes.explanation: UV always runs from 0 to 1 whatever the image size, so shader code never needs the pixel count.

quizzes.question: An image lands in a WebGL texture with the wrong v convention. It shows up…
quizzes.explanation: Images put v = 0 at the top, classic WebGL textures at the bottom. Only v differs, so the flip is always vertical.

quizzes.question: A canvas is 4 pixels wide. What is u at the centre of pixel x = 1?
quizzes.explanation: u = (x + 0.5) / W = 1.5 / 4 = 0.375. Without the +0.5 you get the pixel's left edge, 0.25.

quizzes.question: To map u from [0, 1] to NDC, someone writes x = u − 0.5. The drawing…
quizzes.explanation: u − 0.5 only shifts to [−0.5, 0.5], but NDC spans −1 to 1. Stretch by two, then shift: x = 2u − 1.

quizzes.question: Why is y = 1 − 2v rather than 2v − 1?
answers: Image v grows down, NDC y grows up
quizzes.explanation: Images count v down from the top edge; NDC counts y up from the centre, so the sign flips.
